Hostels.title: Housing & residential
Hostels.intro: Rooms for every budget, a mess in every hostel, and a warden on every block. Everything below is from SRM's hostel pages and its 2026–27 fee circulars.
Hostels.accommodationIntro: SRM offers a wide choice of rooms to suit every budget — from AC rooms with attached washrooms to economical shared rooms — on one of India's greenest campuses. Students come from every part of India and many countries.
facilities: Cot, study table, chair and cupboard in every room
Solar hot water, mineral water and water coolers
TV hall and a common reading room
Laundry service (optional, paid with hostel fees)
General stores, food stalls, ATM and bookshops nearby
Prayer halls for Hindus, Muslims and Christians next to the hostels
Dining halls close to every hostel
Hostels.directorRole: Professor and Director (Hostels), Directorate of Hostels, SRMIST Kattankulathur
Hostels.directorQuote: Our mission is to provide a safe, supportive and comfortable living environment that fosters the academic success and personal growth of every SRMISTian.
Hostels.menIntro: SRM lists room for about {n} engineering students across these blocks. Every block has its own warden.
Hostels.womenIntro: SRM lists room for about {n} engineering students across these blocks. Every block has its own warden.
Hostels.womenAmenities: Every room has study tables, chairs, cots and storage lockers. Girls' blocks have purified water, 24×7 CCTV, security guards, round-the-clock Wi-Fi, indoor and outdoor games, a gym, power backup and biometric attendance, with a supermarket, eateries and a photocopy shop on the premises.
Hostels.intlIntro: Two fully air-conditioned hostels for international students, with room for about {n}.

extras.indoorGames: Indoor games: carrom, chess, table tennis
extras.nearJavaGreen: Next to the Java Green food court

applySteps: Finish your admission formalities and get your Student Net ID and password — only then can you book a hostel.
Book online on the student portal when your booking opens. First-year students are told their schedule directly; seniors see it on the portal.
Choose the block and room type you want. You can't pick a specific room number.
Before moving in, sign the undertaking to follow the hostel rules and the code of conduct.
beforeItems: Check your bank account's single-transaction limit — net banking works best.
Read the hostel rules and the code of conduct.
Make sure your internet connection is stable.
duringItems: Log in to the student portal on one device only.
If a payment seems stuck, check the transaction log in your portal before trying again.
afterItems: The undertaking, personal-details and medical forms emailed to you a week before reopening
eligible: Full-time undergraduate, postgraduate and research students of Engineering and Technology, Medicine and Health Sciences, Science and Humanities, Management and Law
Full-time diploma students of Polytechnic and Hotel Management
notEligible: Students who failed and were not re-admitted as regular students
Part-time, evening, correspondence or external students
Working men and women, and former students
Hostels.diningIntro: Every hostel has its own mess for breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner, with North Indian and South Indian menus. The international hostel adds Thai, Chinese and continental food.
Hostels.guestIntro: Tell the hostel office in advance. Guest rates per meal:
messRules: Self-service, with unlimited food except special items.
Show your ID card and mess card at every meal.
No food in rooms — if you're ill, the deputy warden arranges meals.
Wasting food costs ₹500 the first time; repeat offenders can lose their hostel place.
You stay a member of your hostel's mess until you officially leave; you can't switch messes.

Hostels.safetyIntro: What parents ask about most, from SRM's 2026 hostel rules and hostel pages.

safety.d: Girls' hostels have 24×7 CCTV, security guards, power backup and biometric attendance. Every hostel has a biometric in-time set by its warden.
To stay out after 9 PM, a student must tell the warden in writing in advance, with consent from a parent in writing, by email or on a video call.

Parents may visit with the hostel's permission and sign the visitors' book; visitors stay in the lounge. Visitors of the opposite gender, other than parents, are not allowed, and no one stays overnight without approval.
Students use SRM Hospital in working hours and its casualty department after hours. At night the deputy warden arranges help, and an ambulance is on campus 24 hours.
Ragging is a cognisable offence under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Ragging Act, punished with suspension or expulsion.
Only hostellers and authorised staff may enter, and students carry their ID cards at all times. Silence hours are 10 PM to 6 AM.

Hostels.sourceNote: From SRM's hostel pages, 2026–27 fee circulars and 2026 hostel rules, as of 26 October 2026. Fees and rules can change — confirm with the hostel office.

Life.title: Student life
Life.intro: Life at SRM is what you make of it: clubs, fests, sport, service and support, on a green 250-acre campus. Everything here is from SRM's student-life pages.

holistic.lead: SRM's aim is simple: by the time students leave, they should have the self-belief to be whoever they want to be. Student life can be what each student wants it to be.

points.d: Walking and cycling are the most popular ways to move around campus, with security and 24-hour emergency services.
From entertainment to extracurriculars and religious life, the activities are as varied as the students.
All major Indian festivals are celebrated on campus, with special lunches in the hostels.

green.lead: Over 250 acres at Kattankulathur: lakes, gardens, lawns, tree-lined walkways and real biodiversity, kept green and safe by campus policy.

points.d: Roads named after inspiring people, and statues of Raja Raja Chola, Swami Vivekananda, Mahatma Gandhi, Thiruvalluvar and Socrates along the way.
Hundreds of AC and non-AC SRM buses move people around campus and, for those who opt in, to and from Chennai and nearby areas.
Ramps, low-floor buses, lifts to classrooms and labs, battery cars and wheelchair-friendly paths.
A professional security force under a chief security officer, with a surveillance control room, cameras, access control and campus fire safety.

green.policies: Green policies: bicycles first, a ban on plastic, landscaping, pedestrian walkways and restricted car entry.
green.campusLife: Associate Director, Campus Life – Infrastructure & Facilities

affairs.lead: The Directorate of Student Affairs (DSA) runs everything beyond the classroom — clubs, houses, fests, discipline, counselling and student welfare. Of the students, by the students, for the students.

events.rendezvous: A fest of dance, music and fashion
events.josh: Cultural and sports event for faculty
events.butterflies: Cultural and sports day for government-school students

affairs.moreFests: Also on the calendar: Shuru, Tarana and Milan.

diversity.lead: It's a “mini India” at SRM: students from every part of India and from around the world, with regional festivals celebrated on campus.
diversity.body: Living and learning together builds confidence, camaraderie and the ability to work in diverse teams. Culture, sport, fine arts and entrepreneurship are all encouraged beyond academics.

counselling.lead: Free, confidential counselling for anything that gets in the way: stress, anxiety, exam pressure, family issues, loneliness, low self-esteem, poor concentration, sleeplessness or thoughts of suicide.

services.d: Counselling for personal problems that affect studies and campus life, offered for over 13 years.
Psychiatrists available 24/7, with individual counselling and therapy for students and staff.

Psychological assessment and therapy (CBT, mindfulness and more) for anxiety, sleep, procrastination, relationships and addictions, including smartphone addiction. SRM Hospital, D-Block extension, 5th floor.
SRM's mental-health app, with anonymous, round-the-clock online counselling through YourDOST.

services.t: Wellness Centre and University Wellness Programme
services.d: Fitness and diet routines with doctors and dieticians, and campus-wide wellbeing campaigns by the School of Public Health.

counselling.urgent: In crisis right now? Call Tele-MANAS, the Government of India's free 24×7 mental-health line, on <tel>{n}</tel>.

community.lead: Students are drawn into community service from their first year.

items.d: A school on campus for drop-outs and the children of construction workers — 32 children, taught by SRM students in the evenings.
Sports, literary and cultural days for children from 25 government and private schools around Kattankulathur.
A canteen in the women's hostel run by a women's self-help group, guided by the NGO Hand in Hand.

community.impact: What students take away: leadership, a sense of responsibility, self-esteem, and the discovery that they can make a difference.

clubs.lead: Fifteen student-run clubs, open to everyone, with workshops, sessions and competitions all year.

rotaract.d: Community service with the Rotary Club of Meenambakkam, towards the sustainable development goals.

astrophilia.d: Stars, planets and galaxies: astronomy talks and discussions.

music.d: Perform, jam and learn with fellow musicians.

literature.d: Readers and writers: poetry, stories and essays.

festival.d: Celebrating the festivals of every culture on campus.

dance.d: Every style, for beginners and trained dancers alike.

dramatics.d: Acting, stagecraft and the performing arts.

sports.d: Training and competitions across sports, all year.

women.d: Awareness, symposiums and camps on gender equality.

social.d: Volunteering, social service and awareness camps.

antiRagging.lead: Ragging is a criminal offence. SRM condemns it in every form: seniors welcome freshers with flowers and advice, and every incident is acted on.
antiRagging.helpTitle: If you see or face ragging
what: Teasing or rudeness towards a fresher, in words, writing or action
Making a student do something that causes shame, torment or embarrassment
Disrupting a fresher's studies, or making them do others' academic work
Demanding money, or forcing someone to spend
Physical or sexual abuse, or anything that endangers health
Insults by email, post or in public, or anything that harms mental health or self-confidence
punish: An FIR with the police for every incident
Cancellation of admission, or expulsion and a bar on admission elsewhere
Suspension from classes, exams or the hostel; results withheld
Collective punishment when the culprits aren't identified

antiDiscrimination.lead: SRMIST works to give every student and staff member an environment of freedom and dignity.
antiDiscrimination.body: Anyone who feels humiliated or targeted because of caste can lodge a complaint in the prescribed form. It goes to a senior official and is followed by an enquiry.

religious.lead: Places of worship on campus, and the festivals celebrated at each.

temple.d: Vinayagar Chathurthi, Pongal, Sankatahara Chathurthi, Deepavali, Navarathri (10 days), Pournami, Karthigai, New Year's Day, Tamil New Year

church.d: New Year's Day, Good Friday, Easter, Christmas

eoc.lead: The Equal Opportunity Cell makes sure everyone — whatever their caste, gender, disability, background or identity — has equal access to opportunities, resources and support.

items.d: Confidential guidance for anyone facing a difficult situation, and help reaching the right resources.
Workshops and seminars on diversity, equity and inclusion.
Works with administrators and faculty on policies that remove barriers.
Engages students, staff and families to build a culture of belonging.

Life.sourceNote: From SRM's student-life pages, as of 27 October 2026. Contacts can change — check SRM's site before you call.

Centres.title: Research centres
Centres.intro: Ten central laboratories and facilities, open across colleges, where SRM's research is done: from Siddha medicine to supercomputing, from zero-cement concrete to earthquake prediction. Each one below in brief, with who to contact.

iiism.name: Interdisciplinary Institute of Indian System of Medicine
iiism.brief: Research that validates and standardises herbal medicines from Siddha, Ayurveda and Unani. IIISM works with Banaras Hindu University, has MoUs with AYUSH and the Central Council for Research in Ayurveda and Siddha, and has 200 acres set aside to propagate medicinal plants.
facilities: Drug testing laboratory for Indian medicine

reach.name: Centre for Research in Environment, Sustainability Advocacy and Climate Change
reach.brief: Environment, sustainable development, advocacy and climate change, guided by the UN Sustainable Development Goals, with partners in academia, industry, start-ups and funding agencies who rely on it for technical, policy and regulatory support.
focus: How pesticides, industrial chemicals and plasticisers move through India's urban hotspots
Long-range air transport of persistent organic pollutants
Plasticisers in India's rivers and seas
Low-cost clean-up of emerging contaminants in soil, water and wastewater
facilities: Environmental science and technology lab: water, wastewater and air testing

nrc.name: Nanotechnology Research Centre
nrc.brief: Nanoscience for energy, the environment and healthcare, with labs for synthesis, characterisation, fabrication and computational modelling. Collaborators include Shizuoka University, Université Paris Cité, KTH Sweden, NIMS Japan, BARC, IIT Madras and NPL, and industry partners Ashok Leyland and the Rane Group.

cacr.name: Centre for Advanced Concrete Research
cacr.brief: Portland cement carries a lot of embodied carbon dioxide. CACR develops lower-carbon concretes from industrial wastes such as fly ash and slag, with nano-materials — including geopolymer concretes that need no Portland cement at all.
focus: Railway sleepers and pavers with new binders
highlights: A zero-cement concrete building on campus
Geopolymer paver blocks, pavements and roads

dbt.name: SRM-DBT Platform for Advanced Life Science Technologies
dbt.brief: A national core facility set up with the Department of Biotechnology, Government of India, offering research services and skills training in modern life sciences to SRM and outside researchers.
highlights: One-year Postgraduate Diploma in Genetic Counselling, built on the competencies of the US Accreditation Council for Genetic Counseling

mrc.name: Division of Medical Research
mrc.brief: Basic and clinical research in medical and allied sciences, PhD research and research-methodology courses for faculty and students, with a central laboratory, an animal house and an Institutional Ethics Committee.
highlights: BIRAC BioNEST grant of about ₹10 crore (2024, five years) for a biotech innovation ecosystem
DBT project on Cryptosporidium infection, ₹41.5 lakh (2023)
ICMR multisite study on spotting early-childhood developmental disorders, ₹1.02 crore (2023)

statistics.name: Centre for Statistics
statistics.brief: SRM's hub for statistical training, research and consultancy: helping students, scholars and faculty turn research questions into sound analysis.
facilities: Statistical Training Unit: short courses for internal and external participants
Data Analytic Unit: research questions into statistical problems
Statistical Consultancy Unit (fee-based): grant writing, questionnaires, survey design, analysis and reports
focus: Basic statistics and biostatistics with SPSS
Systematic review and meta-analysis with R

eqrc.name: Earthquake Research Cell
eqrc.brief: Set up in July 2012 to study the causes, occurrence and prediction of earthquakes, and to build simulation models for prediction, prevention and damage reduction. Field work covers the Sikkim–Darjeeling Himalaya and the North East, the Andaman region, the Ponnaiyar basin in South India and Gujarat.

hpcc.name: High Performance Computing Centre
hpcc.brief: SRM's supercomputing facility, open to any SRMIST faculty member or student who registers. It runs three clusters — STAR, COMET and GALAXY — plus GENOME and MOON servers and workstations.

scif.name: SRM Central Instrumentation Facility
scif.brief: One place to find and book the Directorate of Research's state-of-the-art instruments. Open to SRMIST researchers and to industry and academic users outside SRM, with published service charges.

patents.lead: Inventions from SRM's labs, protected in India and abroad, and some already licensed to industry.
